plan_a_advantages: More frequent long runs at easy effort, potentially beneficial for building overall mileage and endurance.

plan_b_advantages: Includes dedicated tempo and hill work for targeted speed and strength development.
More race-specific long runs that simulate the demands of a trail race, improving pacing and endurance at a moderate effort.
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates more targeted intensity work and race-specific simulation. While Plan A focuses heavily on building a strong aerobic base with long, easy runs, Plan B includes a dedicated tempo run and hill repeats, directly addressing the need for improved sustainable effort and climbing power – key components of trail speed. Furthermore, Plan B’s longer runs, particularly the 31.5km run, more closely mimic the demands of a typical trail race, providing valuable experience in pacing and endurance at a moderate effort. Plan A’s longer runs are consistently at an easy pace, which, while beneficial for building volume, doesn’t provide the same stimulus for speed development.
